The test failed in the method containsAny(CharSequence cs, char[] searchChars). The test uses two supplementary Unicode characters represented as surrogate pairs:

- CharU20000 = "\uD840\uDC00" (U+20000)
- CharU20001 = "\uD840\uDC01" (U+20001)

The test asserts that containsAny(CharU20000, CharU20001.toCharArray()) returns false. This means it is testing if the string containing the supplementary character U+20000 contains any character from a char array representation of U+20001.

Looking at the code of containsAny:

- It takes each character (16-bit char) from the CharSequence cs and checks if it matches any character in the searchChars array.
- The variable ch is assigned cs.charAt(i), which is a single char (16 bits).
- It compares ch with each char in searchChars.
- Since supplementary characters in UTF-16 are represented by surrogate pairs (two chars), checking character by character will not correctly handle supplementary characters.
- The method does not treat surrogate pairs as a single character, so the search is done on individual chars rather than full code points.
- In the test, the string CharU20000 is actually two chars (a high surrogate and a low surrogate), and CharU20001.toCharArray() will be two chars as well; so the containsAny compares their individual chars rather than the full supplementary character.
- This will cause incorrect matching or no matching between the supplementary characters, failing the expectation in the test.

In summary, the root cause is that containsAny uses charAt(i) and compares chars directly. This does not support supplementary characters correctly, which consist of two chars (surrogate pairs) representing a single Unicode code point above U+FFFF.

The issue report summary and description confirm this diagnosis: StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly, using an example with U+20000.

The method containsAny needs to be adjusted to properly handle supplementary characters, e.g., by iterating over code points rather than chars.

No relevant recent bug reports appear to relate to this Unicode supplementary character handling issue. The related reports are about unrelated features or documentation.

# Diagnosis

The bug occurs because StringUtils.containsAny processes the CharSequence and char[] inputs at the 16-bit char granularity using charAt(i) and direct char comparison. Supplementary Unicode characters above U+FFFF are encoded as surrogate pairs (two 16-bit chars), so the method fails to correctly identify matches of these characters as single Unicode points. This leads to incorrect or failed matches when supplementary characters are involved, as demonstrated by the failing test with U+20000 and U+20001 supplementary characters.

The root cause is improper handling of supplementary Unicode characters by not iterating over code points (int) but over individual chars (16-bit), causing the method to treat surrogate halves as separate characters rather than as one full character.
